title: partner-offer-template-and-integration-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight playbook + working template for packaging partner offers for cloud marketplaces. Focus is to reduce back-and-forth between partner engineering and sales/legal by giving one canonical set of offer templates, a minimal technical acceptance checklist, and copy/snippet variants ready for tile/listing pages.

Audience:
- Partner GTM / alliances reps preparing a listing or co-sell offer
- Solutions/partner engineers who need to prepare the integration artifacts
- Marketplace ops and legal for acceptance gating

Principles / constraints:
- Keep the initial offer simple: 1 SKU for trial / dev, 1 SKU for production (metered or reserved). Avoid >3 SKUs unless partner provides clear separation (e.g., enterprise vs platform).
- Make the tile copy scan-friendly: 1-line summary, 3 bullets, 1 demo CTA. Tile headline <= 60 chars, short description <= 160 chars.
- Technical acceptance should be automatable where possible (smoke test endpoint, sample app).
- Support at least English + one major local language (customer region) for launch; add full i18n later.

Offer templates (pick one as starting point):
A) Self-serve SaaS Connector (metered usage)
- SKU naming: partnername-connector-usage
- Billing model: per invocation / per token equivalent (if relevant). Provide conversion guidance (tokens -> calls).
- Trial: 30-day free credits, auto-enroll via marketplace trial flow.
- Example tile headline: "PartnerX Connector for Redwood — Secure LLM inference in your cloud"
- Short bullets (tile): "Plug into your data lake, Low-latency inference routing, Pay-as-you-go pricing"

B) Reserved Capacity / Dedicated Offer
- SKU naming: partnername-dedicated-monthly
- Billing model: monthly reservation (vGPU-hours or instance-commit). Include burst pricing policy.
- Trial: short-term pilot (30–90 days) with limited throughput.
- Tile headline example: "PartnerX Dedicated: predictable GPU clusters for inference"

C) Hybrid (managed + private bundle)
- SKU naming: partnername-managed-private
- Billing model: platform license + infra consumption
- Requires more legal review (data residency, audit clauses)

Listing copy rules and examples:
- Headline (60 char max): value-forward, no jargon. Example: "Fast, secure LLM inference for regulated apps"
- Short description (up to 160 chars): one-sentence benefit + CTA. Example: "Connect your data and run low-latency LLMs. Free trial and enterprise SLA available."
- 3 bullets: security, performance, integration. Example bullets: "SOC2-ready deployment options", "Sub-200ms median latency for typical prompts", "Out-of-the-box connectors for S3, Snowflake, and Postgres"
- Long description (300–800 chars): 3–4 paragraphs. Include architecture diagram link, expected latencies under typical workloads, and recommended usage patterns.

Assets required for submission (minimum):
- 1x high-res tile image (1200x627 PNG), transparent logo SVG, screenshot of product, short explainer video (optional but recommended)
- 1-pager PDF (one page) with feature bullets, deployment options, pricing summary, and contact info
- Demo credentials (or self-demo flow) and postman/curl sample calls for smoke tests

Technical acceptance checklist (smoke-level, run by partner or partner-eng):
- Public endpoint or partner-hosted demo exists (https) with sample payloads
- Authentication: OAuth2 client credentials / marketplace-provided token exchange documented
- Example POST call and response documented with sample code (curl, python)
- Error handling defined (rate limit status codes, retry windows)
- Telemetry hooks: logs or sample traces showing latency and error rate (for observability review)
- Data handling notes: where inputs/outputs are stored, retention, and redaction patterns
- Security docs: SOC2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS integration notes
- Network: list of egress IPs or support for private endpoints (VPC peering or private links)
- Packaging: Docker image tags (if partner provides deployable), or detailed manifest for 1-click deployment (CloudFormation/Terraform snippets)

Acceptance gates (operational):
- Gate 1 (Security): SOC2 attestation or equivalent + basic pen-test summary
- Gate 2 (Functionality): Successful smoke test (3 sample calls) and correct auth flow
- Gate 3 (Billing): SKU mapping validated and e2e charge test in sandbox environment
- Gate 4 (Assets): All tile copy, images, and 1-pager uploaded to marketplace portal

Localization & accessibility notes:
- Localize headline + short description for target region (EN + 1 regional language at launch). Keep translations terse and reviewed by native reviewer.
- Provide alt text for all images, transcript for videos, and ensure color contrast on screenshots

Common integration pitfalls (notes from engineering):
- Missing retry semantics: many partners forget to document exponential backoff windows and idempotency keys.
- Billing mismatch: partners often send a different metric (calls vs tokens) than marketplace expects; include a mapping table.
- Expect truncation: demo inputs sometimes exceed max token length—provide clear guidance and sample truncation logic.

Sample SKU-to-Marketplace mapping table (template to copy into spreadsheet):
- partner_sku_id, marketplace_sku_id, metric_type, unit, pricing_unit_description, trial_credits
- Example row: partnerx-connector-usage, MP-12345, calls, call, "per-API-call (first 50k free)", "$100 credit"

Go-to-market launch playbook (brief timeline):
- Week 0: Kickoff call (partner PM, partner eng, Redwood alliances, marketplace ops). Share this playbook.
- Week 1: Partner prepares assets + demo. Redwood does initial legal review.
- Week 2: Technical smoke test + billing sandbox mapping.
- Week 3: Final assets uploaded to marketplace portal. Partner fixes any acceptance issues.
- Week 4: Launch window; coordinate co-marketing assets and press/announce plan

Roles & ownership (suggested):
- Partner: demo + engineering support, billing mapping, tile assets
- Redwood alliances: primary contact, legal triage, go/no-go decision for marketplace submission
- Marketplace ops: acceptance tests, SKU registration, final publishing
- Solutions engineering: provide sample integration code and review performance expectations

Unresolved questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Do we require full SOC2 for all partners or accept attestations for lower-risk connectors? (open, legal to weigh in)
- Billing granularity vs UX: fine-grained metering is accurate but complicates SKU mapping and customer invoices. Is a bundled per-seat or per-instance model preferable for ease of purchase?

Examples: ready-to-copy tile snippets
- Variant A (developer-focused): "Integrate PartnerX for real-time data-enriched LLM responses — quick setup, predictable pricing."
- Variant B (enterprise-focused): "Enterprise-grade inference with private networking and SLA-backed throughput."
- CTA examples: "Try free", "Request enterprise trial", "See integration guide"

Launch checklist (short actionable):
- [ ] Create partner SKU in internal catalog + map to marketplace SKU
- [ ] Upload tile image, logo, and 1-pager to portal
- [ ] Provide demo account + smoke test credentials
- [ ] Run billing sandbox charge and verify invoice flow
- [ ] Legal sign-off on data and security clauses
- [ ] Publish and validate live tile (QA flow: open tile, run demo call, verify telemetry)

Next steps (for this doc):
- Convert SKU mapping template into a shared spreadsheet and send to partner PMs (task: JIRA-OPS-4821)
- Create a short recording walkthrough of the tile copy rules (owner: Marcus)
- Schedule a recurring 30-min intake call for new partner listings (owner: Sofia)

Notes: keep this doc intentionally lightweight. The goal is to reduce churn during early listing stages. For complex or regulated offers we should route partners to the full marketplace onboarding SOP (CONFLUENCE-1234).
